description: GMIA-NEXT is a 30-metre global map of irrigated cropland for the 2023-2024 growing season, released as a successor in name to the FAO Global Map of Irrigation Areas. It provides an irrigation probability map and a binary irrigated or not irrigated map, derived with machine learning from several Earth observation and environmental datasets; the ground truth used for training and validation is published in a separate repository. It was produced by researchers at the universities of Delaware, Oklahoma and Tennessee and published on Zenodo in June 2026 (version 0) under CC BY 4.0 as continental GeoTIFF tiles of several gigabytes each. Caveats: it covers a single recent season, it is a first version, and accuracy varies by region and by the classifier's threshold. Simulation uses: locating irrigated demand for irrigation infrastructure and capacity planning, and drought and climate adaptation studies. Related records: the FAO Global Map of Irrigation Areas (data-fao-global-map-of-irrigation-areas) and GMIE (data-gmie-global-maximum-irrigation-extent).
